subject: Local provenance and derivative access safeguards
messages:
From: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@greenbridgeanalytics.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenbridgeanalytics.com
Date: Sun, 5 Jul 2026 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: GreenBridge — operational proof for non-training / derivative rights

Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the product walkthrough last week. As we move toward legal review / procurement we need concrete operational evidence for a few items in scope for our DPA and security questionnaire:

- A firm commitment that tenant data (prompts + returned responses) will not be used to improve or retrain any foundation models (a machine-learning "no-training" guarantee) unless we opt in.
- Operational controls that show how prompt/response data is segregated, how ephemeral KV/prefix caching behaves, and how long any runtime logs are retained.
- A current list of subprocessors involved in text ingest, logging, and storage, and whether any of those subprocessors are outside the EU.
- If data export is required for audit, we need an export path (SFTP or signed API export), and evidence you can support onshore KMS or key residency for EU accounts.

Can you provide the above as an evidence pack (preferably PDF/CSV) and a short note on proposed DPA addendum language for derivative/ownership clauses? Procurement is on copy — they want this by next Tuesday.

Thanks,

Sara Lowe
Head of Security, GreenBridge Analytics
Sara.Lowe@greenbridgeanalytics.com
+44 20 5555 1212

--
GreenBridge Analytics | Confidential
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@greenbridgeanalytics.com>
Cc: procurement@greenbridgeanalytics.com, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 09:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GreenBridge — operational proof for non-training / derivative rights

Hi Sara — thanks for the clear list. Short answer: we can cover each ask, and I attached a concise package that teams can consume during vendor review. Details below and attachments: no-train-operational-controls.pdf (controls and retention tables) and subprocessor-list-2026-07.csv.

Summary of controls (high level):
- Contractual commitment: Redwood will include an explicit DPA addendum with a model-improvement opt-out clause that prevents using Customer data for training or model updates unless the customer provides written opt-in.
- Runtime isolation: incoming requests are routed to tenant-scoped containers with ephemeral KV cache. KV/prefix caches are marked ephemeral and cleared within 2 hours by default; retention can be configured to 0 for EU Dedicated/Private customers.
- Logging minimization: production token telemetry required for billing/latency is aggregated and pseudo-anonymized; request/response payloads are not retained in plain text in long-term logs for no-train tenants.
- Subprocessor map: the CSV lists storage, monitoring, and orchestration vendors; entries outside EU are flagged. We can offer onshore replicas for storage where required.
- Export path: we support signed API export and SFTP exports to a customer-controlled endpoint. We will provide a proof export sample (manifest + checksum) for your test tenant.
- KMS & key residency: for Private/Dedicated accounts we support customer-managed keys (AWS KMS/HSM). For hosted EU accounts we can provide onshore KMS routing under an enterprise addendum.

Operational evidence timeline:
- Today: attachments (controls + subprocessor list) for your security team.
- By EOD Tue (2026-07-07): sample SFTP export and a short attestation template for your legal team to sign-off.
- Next week: if you want, Jonas can run a 30-minute technical walkthrough / live demo showing cache eviction and export.

Two quick clarifying questions:
1) Do you need the retention/eviction figures to be locked in the DPA (hard SLAs) or is an operational commitment sufficient?
2) Will procurement prefer an onshore KMS OR a customer-managed KMS (both supported, different contract flows)?

I'll loop Jonas for the detailed technical attestation.

Best,
Kimberly Park
Director, Trust & Compliance
Redwood Inference
kimberly.park@redwood.ai

Attachments: no-train-operational-controls.pdf, subprocessor-list-2026-07.csv
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@greenbridgeanalytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenbridgeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 6 Jul 2026 18:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GreenBridge — operational proof for non-training / derivative rights

Sara / team — quick technical notes to supplement Kimberly's packet. I've attached an attestation-template.docx that we can pre-fill and sign once GreenBridge confirms the controls you need.

Technical detail highlights (for your architects):
- Ephemeral KV mechanics: the runtime keeps per-session KV in-memory; explicit eviction occurs on session close or after the configured TTL. For hosted no-train customers we set TTL=0 (write-through disabled) by policy flag.
- Tokenization / telemetry: per-token latencies are recorded but hashed + aggregated at the instance level before being sent to metrics collectors; raw request/response streams are not captured in persistent observability indexes for opt-out tenants.
- Derivative artifacts & sandboxing: any model outputs that are stored for customer workflows are saved to tenant-scoped storage with access controls and can be included in a customer export snapshot. We can optionally perform output redaction or redaction hooks prior to export.
- Attestation mechanics: we can provide a signed attestation stating the tenant_flag=no_training was applied, list the control checks executed, and include checksums for any exported manifests.

If you'd like, we can schedule the 30-minute demo Tue afternoon (UTC) to show eviction in a live session and run a trial export to a GreenBridge SFTP target.

Jonas Weber
Staff Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

Attachments: attestation-template.docx
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Lowe <sara.lowe@greenbridgeanalytics.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@greenbridgeanalytics.com
Date: Tue, 7 Jul 2026 09:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: GreenBridge — operational proof for non-training / derivative rights

Hi Sara / procurement team — I circulated Kimberly's controls to Legal. Below is a short draft clause we propose for the DPA addendum; happy to redline per your counsel. I'll attach a formal draft (dpa-addendum-draft.docx) for your checklist.

Draft addendum excerpt: 
"Customer Data Use and Model Improvement
1. Redwood agrees not to use Customer Data (including prompts, uploaded files, and model responses) to train, fine-tune, or improve any models that are generally available or used by third parties, unless Customer provides prior written consent (Opt-In).
2. For avoidance of doubt, telemetry necessary for system reliability (aggregated, non-identifiable performance metrics) may be collected; such telemetry will not include raw request/response payloads for Customers who have activated the Opt-Out.
3. Redwood shall provide, upon Customer request, an attestation of the controls applied and a machine-checkable export of data and manifests (SFTP or signed API) within the timeframe set out in Schedule A.
4. Subprocessors engaged in processing Customer Data will be disclosed in the Subprocessor Schedule; Customer may request onshore processing or additional contractual assurances when subprocessors are located outside the Customer's region.
"

Implementation notes: we recommend Schedule A set the attestation turnaround to 10 business days for an initial export and 30 business days for deeper forensic exports. If you need shorter SLAs we can discuss an enterprise add-on.

Action items I propose now:
- Kimberly/Jonas: provide the sample SFTP export + manifest by EOD Tue as proposed.
- GreenBridge: confirm whether the retention TTL should be codified as an SLA in Schedule A or accepted as an operational commitment.
- Procurement: confirm PO / procurement timeline so Legal can align execution.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
david.kim@redwood.ai

Attachments: dpa-addendum-draft.docx

Thanks all — this is helpful. Procurement has asked me to confirm a few final items before we route to our external counsel: 

1) Please send the SFTP export sample and manifest to procurement@greenbridgeanalytics.com by EOD Tue (we'll validate checksum and schema).
2) Please include the subprocessor CSV filtered for any processors outside the EU and note which ones you can replace with onshore alternatives (if any).
3) We prefer the retention TTL to be codified in Schedule A for auditability (initial ask: eviction within 2 hours OR permanent no-retention flag).
4) For KMS: GreenBridge requires either (a) Redwood route keys to an EU KMS we control or (b) Redwood provide onshore KMS routing with contractual attestations. Which of these is fastest from your side?

If you can get the SFTP sample + attestation template filled and a redline of the DPA excerpt into procurement's inbox by EOD Tue, we can get external counsel review started Wed and aim to finalize next week.

PO reference: GB-PROC-2026-0707 (procurement on copy).

Best,
Sara Lowe
Head of Security, GreenBridge Analytics
